title: 14 BORING Businesses That Run Without a Single Employee

speakers.name: Harry (illustrative composite character narrated by host)

promo_conflict: No sponsor or product pitch remains. 'Harry' looks like an invented composite character: in part one he works a rec-centre front desk and in part two he is an office-park facilities coordinator. His numbers (e.g. $3,919/month, $6,129/month) are narrated, not first-hand. Most figures are aggregated or second-hand US data.

stated_problem.quote: for the privilege of doing it where nobody can hear them
stated_problem.speaker: Narrator

idea.name: Unstaffed karaoke booth
idea.one_liner: A private karaoke room put inside a bowling alley or bar on revenue share, booked online by the hour and opened with keypad codes that expire.
idea.customer: Groups of friends on evenings out
idea.offer: Private karaoke room rented by the hour or 30-minute slot
idea.revenue_model: Hourly/30-min room rental; 20-30% revenue share to the host venue

key_quotes.quote: You offer the host a share of the takings instead of rent, somewhere in the 20 to 30% range
A keypad lock gets fitted, and every booking generates a code that dies at the end of the slot.
Price the unit the customer actually wants to buy, not the unit that is easiest to bill.

claims.quote: A private room rents for 30 to 150 dollars an hour, depending on the town and the night.
Weekday afternoons run 10 to 20% under it.
One booth, booked around 11 hours a week at 50 dollars an hour, brings in roughly 1800 dollars a month.

claims.claim: With drinks and snacks, operators report $1,100-4,000 per week
claims.quote: Operators who pair the room with drinks and snacks report far higher, in the range of 1100 to 4000 dollars in a single week.
A room like that costs about 15 dollars an hour to run.
You offer the host a share of the takings instead of rent, somewhere in the 20 to 30% range

claims.claim: Busy bowling alley has 300-500 people passing on a Friday
claims.quote: A busy bowling alley walks 300 to 500 people past that door on a Friday night.
Spinners in Maroochydore runs a karaoke room at $50 an hour
Months 1 and 2, a karaoke booth on a revenue share in a bowling alley, $300 to $500 while the listing built up reviews.
By month 5, around 900 to 1,300.

claims.claim: Harry's three units blended to ~$3,919/month by month 18
claims.quote: By month 18, blended across three units, he was at about $3,919 a month.

acquisition_channels.details: The host venue (bowling alley/bar) sends its own regulars
Local search for 'karaoke room near me'

ideas.delivery: Booth installed in the host venue. Online booking calendar and keypad codes per booking, with 15-min buffers between slots. Needs a revenue-share deal with a local venue, and someone (or the host) has to reset and clean the room.

tools: keypad smart lock with expiring codes

ideas.other_uk_rules: Licensing Act 2003 (regulated entertainment, which the host's premises licence must cover); PRS for Music/PPL music licensing; UK GDPR for booking data.

idea.name: Nap pod on revenue share
idea.one_liner: A single bookable sleep pod in a hospital, airport, campus or co-working floor, rented by the hour to shift workers.
idea.customer: Hospital staff, airline crew, night workers, students
idea.revenue_model: Hourly rental plus extras; revenue share with host

key_quotes.quote: You buy one unit, and one unit only, and you place it on a revenue share inside a building that already has the crowd.
Utilization, not the sticker price, is what decides this.

claims.quote: A pod rents for 10 to $50 an hour.
Airport pods sit at the top, 25 to 50.
A napping pod startup in the Seattle area opened at 10 to $12 an hour.

claims.claim: Mature operators make $45-65 per occupied hour
claims.quote: Mature operators, once they add extras, report revenue per occupied hour of 45 to $65.
a mid-sized hospital runs somewhere between 1,500 and 4,000 staff across three shifts.
A pod at $20 an hour, booked 5 hours a day, is around $3,000 a month before costs.

claims.quote: Four pods [music] at 70% occupancy earning about $1,000 a month equivalent

acquisition_channels.details: Revenue-share placement in a hospital, airport, campus or co-working floor where the crowd already is

ideas.delivery: QR/app check-in, lock released for the booking, occupancy sensor. Disposable linens or a contract cleaner on a route. Needs a placement deal with an institution.

claims.quote: There is an equipment-led route with as little as 8 to 25,000 dollars down and monthly payments under two to three thousand
